newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start.

text.p: High techs are expected to lead Wall Street stocks higher at the start Tuesday after Motorola Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc reported better than forecast first quarter earnings.

"These two companies have surprised the Street, and that will build further confidence in the rest of the high tech group," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "The group has been battered recently and questions have been raised as to whether it was heading lower."
On Monday, the stock market extended a bounce from Friday, which itself came on the heels of two weeks of trading in which the Dow lost more than 278 points.
"We are still going through a bounce from our lows. We had a correction, and now we are having a technical rally," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.

"The rally faded yesterday in terms of the Dow, but the breadth figures were good. Advanced Micro and Motorola will be helpful. The focus in the market will be first quarter earnings for the next three weeks."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average rise 306.03 points, or 1.73 percent, to end at 18,021.70.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 1.2 at 4272.9.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Motorola Inc was up 3/4 at 61. Advanced Micro Devices was up 2-1/4 at 43-1/2. Intel Corp was up 7/8 to 146, Texas Instruments Inc was up 1/2 at 86 and International Business Machines Corp was up 1/4 at 132-1/2. Chrysler Corp was up 3/8 at 30-1/4. General Motors Corp was up 1/4 at 54-1/4.
Ford Motor Co was up 1/8 at at 31-3/4. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp was down 1/4 at 30-7/8 and Philip Morris Cos Inc fell 1/2 to 112-5/8.
The dollar retreated slightly against the yen in Tokyo and was firm but off its peaks in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly lower, with the long bond down 5/32 to yield 7.08 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that investors scrambled to snap up shares of midsize, specialty securities companies yesterday after news that Bankers Trust New York plans to buy Alex. Brown Inc.
The New York Times Market Place also writes about the deal, saying that Bankers Trust is betting the health care and high technology industries will continue to prosper and need underwriters.
